headline: A 2023 law requires the FBI to use a team approach for child abuse cases and renews federal grants for children's advocacy centers.
what_it_does: The law requires the Federal Bureau of Investigation to use a multidisciplinary team when it investigates child abuse and related crimes. A multidisciplinary team brings together people from different fields to work on a case. The law also reauthorizes grants for children's advocacy centers, which coordinate how child abuse cases are investigated, treated, and prosecuted.

who_it_affects.group: Children who have been abused and their families
who_it_affects.how: FBI child abuse investigations must use a team approach that includes multiple professional fields.
These centers can receive renewed federal grant funding under the law.

who_it_affects.group: FBI agents and staff who investigate child abuse and related crimes
who_it_affects.how: They must work with a multidisciplinary team when handling these cases.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2023; the official summary does not list any later effective dates.
